newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian firm will gain from Nomura tie-up.
newsitem.headline: Indian firm will gain from Nomura tie-up.

text.p: India's UTI Securities will grow in strength after Japan's Nomura Securities buys a 40 percent stake in the state-run stockbroking and investment firm, analysts and officials said on Friday.

"Nomura is one of Asia's largest securities firm. UTI Securities will gain from Nomura's advanced trading system and research methods," said Aashish Pitale, an analyst with ICICI Securities and Finance Company Ltd (I-Sec).
J.P. Morgan has 40 percent and ICICI has 60 percent in ICICI Securities.
UTI Securities confirmed on Friday that Japan's Nomura Securities Co Ltd was interested in buying a 40 percent equity stake in the state-run firm.
"They have shown interest in buying a 40 percent stake in UTI Securities," M.K. Khanna, managing director of UTI Securities told Reuters by telephone from Bombay.
"The formal agreements are yet to be signed," Khanna said.
Analysts said foreign securities firms preferred to enter the Indian market in tie-up with local partners.
"This proposal is nothing new. The foreign firms don't want to burn their fingers," said an analyst with a foreign investment firm, who asked not to be identified.

UTI Securities is a stockbroking and investment company set up in November 1994 by the Unit Trust of India, the country's largest state-run mutual fund. UTI Securities has accounts of about 90 foreign financial institutions, Khanna said.
UTI Securities has a paid-up capital of 300 million rupees ($8.4 million), he added.
"The proposal will provide intermediary services to Nomura's international clients," Khanna said.
"We will get added capacity to our debt and equity accounts outside India. In the last two years we had a combined debt and equity turnover of about 73 billion rupees ($2.04 billion)," he added.
